html:
The Alabama, or Alibamu, are a Muskogean-speaking people of the Southeast, whose towns stood on the upper Alabama River, in the state that now bears their name.

They were close kin of the Koasati and took part in the loose Muscogee Creek Confederacy. The chronicles of Hernando de Soto mention a people called Alibamo in 1541. In 1717 the French built Fort Toulouse near their towns and traded with them from Louisiana.

When France lost its North American lands in 1763, many Alabama moved west into Louisiana and then Texas. There they joined the Koasati, and today they form the Alabama-Coushatta Tribe of Texas, while others are part of the Alabama-Quassarte Tribal Town in Oklahoma.
sum: The Alabama, or Alibamu, are a Muskogean-speaking people of the Southeast, whose towns stood on the upper Alabama River, in the state that now bears their name.
